vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostCu.from: Absolute path to the shell executable used by host-managed terminals. Normally pushed by the connected VS Code client from `terminal.integrated.agentHostProfile.<os>` (falling back to `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.<os>`); when unset, the agent host falls back to the system shell. Only the path is supported; `args` and `env` from the workbench profile are not piped through yet. The workbench only pushes this for the local agent host — remote agent host operators should set this directly in the remote machine's `agent-host-config.json`.
vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostCu.to: Absolute path to the shell executable used by host-managed terminals. Normally pushed by the connected Cognify IDE client from `terminal.integrated.agentHostProfile.<os>` (falling back to `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.<os>`); when unset, the agent host falls back to the system shell. Only the path is supported; `args` and `env` from the workbench profile are not piped through yet. The workbench only pushes this for the local agent host — remote agent host operators should set this directly in the remote machine's `agent-host-config.json`.

vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/session.from: Created In lists the applications that created sessions, grouped by This Computer, Cloud, and each remote host, with the environment in each application's name. Only applications from included environments are listed. Excluding an environment hides its applications without changing their selections; including it again restores them. Other list filters do not remove application choices. Included remote hosts retain their applications while cached sessions remain, even when disconnected. If no environments are included, select an environment first.

If no environments are included, select an environment first.

vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/session.from: The Environment, Created In, and Harness submenus filter the Sessions list. Checked options are included. Reset Filters restores these defaults and shows an Undo notice at the bottom of the Sessions list that restores your previous filters. On desktop, Compact View and Collapse All Groups are available from the Sessions More Actions menu. On phone, use Sort and Find to navigate the list.

vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/action.from: A model's detail page has a heading for each section; the first, the model's name, also gives the model's state, such as Ready or Downloading 41%. Its header has icon buttons named after the model; Tab reaches them and Left and Right Arrow move between them. The first shows the state and what it does: Load for a model that isn't loaded, which loads it right away; Resume while it is paused; Stop while it is loaded; and while the model is busy, an in-progress indicator named with the state and the action that stops it, such as Loading, Cancel, or Downloading 41%, Pause, or Cancel while a model change waits for running responses, which keeps the loaded model. Once chosen, it reads Pausing, Cancelling or Stopping and can't be chosen again until the state changes. Then come Update, when an update is available, with its size, and Remove, which asks first. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between its links, buttons, choices and switches, Back to Models to return to the list, and Escape to close the picker. A warning at the top says when this device doesn't have the GPU memory for the model at its context size. To download a model, its page states the download size, the free space needed, the source and the license; choosing Download, or Set Up for model files already on this device, agrees to exactly what the page shows and downloads it in the background. Downloading doesn't need llama.cpp, but loading a model does, and VS Code doesn't install it. When no llama-server is set, or the one set doesn't support the model or is too old, loading the model shows an error on its page and in the notice above the chat input, with Get llama.cpp, which opens directions for getting a build that supports the model, Open Settings, which opens the Llama Server Path setting (chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath) to point to its llama-server, and Retry. While a model downloads, its page shows a progress bar and the time remaining. While it loads, the page shows Loading model or Warming up, or Reloading when a new context size loads it again, or Retrying without speculative decoding, and why, when this llama.cpp build crashed with it, and, when an earlier load of the same model and context size took a known time, a progress bar and the time remaining estimated from it, which counts down and reads Almost done once that time has passed; a screen reader hears when the step changes. An installed model's page has an Effort Level choice when the model supports it, which sets its effort level for this chat, like a cloud model's effort level, without reloading it; the row and the readout show the new level. It also has a Context choice of the model's context sizes, each read with the GPU memory it needs. Changing the context size of a loaded model reloads it right away without asking, once its running responses finish; for a model that isn't loaded, it applies the next time it loads. In these choices, use the arrow keys to move between options, then Enter or Space to choose one. The page also has the Use in Auto switch, which lets Auto run some requests on this device with cloud fallback. The page updates in place as the model's state changes, and a change of state is announced.
